definition: Classifying social-media accounts as automated bots using behavioral and network signals — an early social-integrity ML task.
details: Classifying social-media accounts as automated bots using behavioral and network signals — an early social-integrity ML task.

explainer.lead: Twitter bot detection is the task of classifying social-media accounts as automated bots using behavioural and network signals. It matters as an early social-integrity ML problem.

tiers.eli5: It is spotting fake accounts that post automatically by looking at how they behave and who they connect to.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers combine activity patterns, timing and follower graphs into classifiers for platform integrity. A pitfall is that bots adapt and accounts drift, so models degrade and can misclassify genuine users.
tiers.paperLevel: It is framed as binary classification of accounts from behavioural and network features. Known limit: labels are noisy and adversarial behaviour shifts the distribution over time.

explainer.example: An account posting at rigid intervals with a dense cluster of similar followers is flagged as automated.
